- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.16) and model forecasts are high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >73), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average for smoothing.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.27) and model is low, avoid underreacting — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.  
- Model often overestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 65, adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
